mcqs.q: The three pairs of MAJOR salivary glands are the:
mcqs.explain: The major salivary glands are the parotid, submandibular and sublingual; the labial/buccal/palatal/lingual glands are minor glands.

mcqs.q: Salivary glands are classified as:
mcqs.explain: Salivary glands are exocrine glands that pour saliva into the oral cavity through ducts.

mcqs.q: The major salivary glands produce about what proportion of saliva?
mcqs.explain: The major glands produce the bulk of saliva (~90%); the numerous minor glands contribute ~10% for continuous lubrication.

mcqs.q: Relative to the parotid gland, the external auditory meatus lies:
mcqs.explain: The external auditory meatus lies above the parotid; below, the gland extends to the angle of the mandible, overlapping the masseter anteriorly and sternomastoid posteriorly.

mcqs.q: Which structure is the MOST superficial of those passing through the parotid gland?
mcqs.explain: From superficial to deep within the parotid: facial nerve, then retromandibular vein, then external carotid artery.

mcqs.q: The facial nerve divides within the parotid into how many terminal branches?
mcqs.explain: The facial nerve enters the posteromedial surface and divides into 5 branches: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, mandibular and cervical.

mcqs.q: The external carotid artery divides within the parotid into the:
mcqs.explain: Within the gland the external carotid artery divides into its two terminal branches — the superficial temporal and maxillary arteries.

mcqs.q: The retromandibular vein is formed within the parotid by union of the:
mcqs.explain: The retromandibular vein is formed by the superficial temporal and maxillary veins; it leaves the lower end and divides into anterior and posterior divisions.

mcqs.q: The parotid duct is also known as:
mcqs.explain: The parotid duct is Stensen's duct; Wharton's duct drains the submandibular gland.

mcqs.q: As it turns medially, the parotid duct pierces which muscle?
mcqs.explain: The duct runs across the masseter, then turns medially to pierce the buccal fat pad, buccopharyngeal fascia, buccinator and buccal mucosa.

mcqs.q: The parotid duct opens into the vestibule opposite the:
mcqs.explain: The duct opens at the parotid papilla in the vestibule, opposite the maxillary (upper) second molar.

mcqs.q: The parotid gland is enclosed by:
opts: Two capsules (a true inner and a false outer from deep cervical fascia)
mcqs.explain: It has an inner (true) connective-tissue capsule and an outer (false) capsule from the investing layer of deep cervical fascia; the tight capsule makes parotid infection very painful.

mcqs.q: Parasympathetic (secretory) supply to the parotid relays in which ganglion?
opts: Otic ganglion (fibres then via the auriculotemporal nerve)
mcqs.explain: Parotid parasympathetic fibres (glossopharyngeal → tympanic plexus → lesser petrosal) relay in the otic ganglion and reach the gland via the auriculotemporal nerve.

mcqs.q: The submandibular gland lies within the:
mcqs.explain: The submandibular gland occupies the submandibular triangle and has true and false capsules.

mcqs.q: The two parts of the submandibular gland are folded around which muscle?
mcqs.explain: The superficial part lies below the mylohyoid and the deep part lies between mylohyoid and hyoglossus.

mcqs.q: The submandibular duct is known as:
mcqs.explain: The submandibular (Wharton's) duct is ~5 cm long and opens at the sublingual papilla beside the lingual frenulum.

mcqs.q: The submandibular duct opens at the:
opts: Sublingual papilla beside the lingual frenulum (floor of mouth)
Vestibule opposite the upper second molar
mcqs.explain: Wharton's duct opens into the floor of the mouth at the sublingual papilla, beside the frenulum of the tongue.

mcqs.q: Which nerves are closely related to the DEEP part of the submandibular gland?
mcqs.explain: The lingual nerve and submandibular ganglion lie above the deep part, and the hypoglossal nerve lies below it — both at risk during gland excision.

mcqs.q: The smallest of the three major salivary glands is the:
mcqs.explain: The sublingual gland is the smallest major gland; it lies under the floor-of-mouth mucosa in the sublingual fold.

mcqs.q: The sublingual gland drains via:
opts: 8–20 small ducts (most opening into the floor of the mouth)
mcqs.explain: The sublingual gland has 8 to 20 small ducts, most opening directly into the floor of the mouth.

mcqs.q: Compared with major glands, MINOR salivary glands are:
mcqs.explain: Minor glands are small, numerous, unencapsulated, scattered in the mucosa/submucosa, each with a short duct opening directly into the cavity.

mcqs.q: Why is parotidectomy a difficult, high-risk operation?
opts: The facial nerve branches run through the gland — risk of facial paralysis
The gland is made of bone
mcqs.explain: The facial nerve and its branches traverse the parotid, so they are at risk of damage (facial paralysis) during parotidectomy.

mcqs.q: The most common BENIGN tumour of the parotid gland is:
mcqs.explain: Pleomorphic adenoma is the commonest benign salivary tumour; the parotid is also the site of mumps (viral parotitis).

mcqs.q: Salivary stones (sialolithiasis) most commonly form in the:
mcqs.explain: Wharton's (submandibular) duct is the commonest site of salivary stones, causing painful swelling at mealtimes.

mcqs.q: A mucocele (small mucous cyst) most commonly arises from:
mcqs.explain: Minor salivary glands (labial, buccal, palatal, lingual) are the common site of mucocele formation.

saqs.q: Name the major and minor salivary glands and their saliva contribution.
saqs.a: Major: parotid, submandibular, sublingual (~90% of saliva). Minor: labial, buccal, palatal, lingual — numerous, unencapsulated (~10%).

saqs.q: List the three structures that pass through the parotid gland, superficial to deep.
saqs.a: Facial nerve (CN VII) → retromandibular vein → external carotid artery. The facial nerve gives 5 branches; the ECA divides into superficial temporal + maxillary arteries.

saqs.q: Describe the course and opening of the parotid (Stensen's) duct.
saqs.a: Runs forward over the masseter below the zygomatic arch, turns medially to pierce the buccal fat pad, buccopharyngeal fascia, buccinator and buccal mucosa, opening at the parotid papilla opposite the upper 2nd molar.

saqs.q: Describe the parts and duct of the submandibular gland.
saqs.a: Two parts around the mylohyoid: superficial (below) and deep (between mylohyoid & hyoglossus). The Wharton's duct opens at the sublingual papilla beside the lingual frenulum; lingual & hypoglossal nerves relate to the deep part.

saqs.q: Outline the parasympathetic supply of the parotid gland.
saqs.a: Glossopharyngeal nerve → tympanic plexus → lesser petrosal nerve → otic ganglion → auriculotemporal nerve → parotid gland (secretomotor).

saqs.q: Compare major and minor salivary glands (4 features).
saqs.a: Major: 3 pairs, encapsulated, long distinct duct, ~90% saliva. Minor: numerous, unencapsulated, short duct, ~10% saliva (continuous lubrication).

saqs.q: List the clinical points for the parotid and the submandibular duct.
saqs.a: Parotid: facial nerve risk in parotidectomy, pleomorphic adenoma, mumps. Submandibular (Wharton's) duct: commonest site of sialolithiasis (stones → painful mealtime swelling); minor glands → mucocele.
